title: "Enterprise Operational Checklists"

# Enterprise Operational Checklists

Maintaining mission-critical Nix and NixOS infrastructure requires discipline, standardized workflows, and proactive operations. The boring default is: **adhering to codified operational checklists for repository structure, CI/CD validation, and fleet maintenance**.

## Mental model

Operational excellence in declarative infrastructure is built on predictability. When every repository follows the same layout, every CI pipeline enforces the same gates, and every server follows the same maintenance lifecycle, human error is eliminated.

## Worked examples

### The Repository Layout Checklist

Every enterprise repository must contain:
1. `flake.nix`: Pure inputs pinned to enterprise platform channel.
2. `flake.lock`: Committed to git; never `.gitignore`d.
3. `shell.nix` / `devShells`: Complete local toolchains for developers.
4. `.envrc`: Containing `use flake` for automatic direnv activation.
5. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: Enforcing `nix flake check`.

### The Pre-Production Deployment Checklist

Before rolling out changes to production nodes:

- [ ] All flake checks pass cleanly (`nix flake check`).
- [ ] No plaintext secrets in `.nix` files (verified via `git grep` and `sops`).
- [ ] `dry-activate` inspected for service restart impacts.
- [ ] Staging environment verified with end-to-end integration tests.
- [ ] Upstream binary cache populated with pre-built closures.
- [ ] Target host has sufficient free disk space (`df -h /nix/store`).

### The Fleet Maintenance Checklist

Executed on a regular monthly schedule:

```bash
# 1. Update channel locks
nix flake update

# 2. Build and verify system closure
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.desk-server.config.system.build.toplevel

# 3. Optimise local and remote stores
nix-store --optimise

# 4. Prune generations older than 30 days
nix-collect-garbage --delete-older-than 30d
```

## The trap

The trap is **treating declarative configurations as self-maintaining**. Without regular garbage collection and lockfile updates, systems accumulate storage overhead and fall behind on security patches.

## The boring rule

- Commit `flake.lock` to git on every repository without exception.
- Run automated security and flake checks on every pull request.
- Schedule recurring maintenance windows for store optimization and input updates.

## Try this

1. Audit your repository against the layout checklist above.
2. Implement an automated workflow that runs `nix-collect-garbage --delete-older-than 30d` on a weekly timer.
